london-things-terms-1.label: Library of Things membership and loan terms

prep.label: Confirm your membership route
prep.text: The operator lists regular, senior, and nonprofit memberships. Check your eligibility, item and collection date with the center.

operators.name: City of Rock Hill Community Toolshed

prep.label: Use the city request route
prep.text: The city lists proof of residency and a tool request form. Check who qualifies and which request to use.

prep.label: Complete the borrower agreement
prep.text: Review the agreement and make a reservation to schedule tool pickup and drop-off.

prep.label: Confirm the organization’s membership
prep.text: First-time borrowers apply as a member agency before ordering. The membership application documents eligibility.

prep.label: Budget for the loan
prep.text: Check the current fee page for handling fees and the due date.

operators.name: Berkeley Public Library Tool Lending Library

prep.label: Register in person
prep.text: Check the library’s proof-of-eligibility instructions. Register in person before placing online holds.

prep.label: Choose a kiosk
prep.text: Reserve an available item online, complete any required identification step and collect it from the assigned kiosk.

tasks.label: Borrow as a household or individual
Borrow without a membership or loan fee
Check membership, deposits and item fees
Check where and when to bring it back

rules.text: The operator offers regular individual membership. Confirm any residency or homeowner conditions before relying on household access.
Most tools have no separate loan charge for current members. The center charges an annual membership fee.
Regular membership is listed at $25 per year. The program lists a separate $50 deposit for high-end tools, with a $20 rental fee deducted.
Rock Hill lists residents alongside neighborhood associations and community organizations. The program is for community maintenance and improvement.
The city lists no charge for eligible borrowers who meet the proof-of-residency requirement.
Request tools using the form on the city’s program page. A request still needs confirmation.
The operator says its tool library is open to local residents.
The program offers free tool checkout to area residents.
One Roof provides a reservation form for pickup and return appointments.
The operator lists a loan of up to one week and schedules drop-off through its reservation process.
The ToolBank lends to eligible organizations. A household acting as an individual does not qualify under this route.
The application has no membership fee. Member agencies pay a tool handling charge for each loan.
The operator’s current fee page lists 5% of each borrowed tool’s retail value per week.
Member agencies order tools online and schedule pickup.
Return the tools clean and dry at the scheduled time. The operator publishes terms of one to eight weeks.
The library lists age and local residency or property-ownership requirements for individual borrowers.
After registering in person, use your library card to place an online hold on an eligible item.
Return the tool by its due date to the Tool Lending Library during open hours.
Individuals can join and reserve items through a membership, subject to the program’s terms.
The program requires a membership and charges published borrowing rates.
Compare the membership options and the charge listed for the item before checkout.
Use the website to find a kiosk and reserve the item.
Return the item to the kiosk where you picked it up by closing time on the stated return date.
